title: terraform(private): consolidate GPU node pools, IAM roles, and VPC state layout for Private deployments
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation: Private deployments have accumulated ad-hoc Terraform fragments for GPU node pools, IAM roles, and VPC/state layout over time. This caused duplication, inconsistent least-privilege IAM, and fragile state migrations when customers upgrade from older installer releases. This PR consolidates reusable modules, introduces a clearer remote state layout, and adds upgrade/migration helpers to reduce operator risk.

Summary of changes: consolidated gpu_node_pool into a single parametrized module with support for GKE/GCP and EKS/AWS variants; created redwood_private_iam module with scoped roles and module-level outputs for service account and role ARNs; refactored networking to a stable vpc_layout module that enforces tagged subnets for control/data planes and documented recommended CIDR sizes; updated state layout to adopt per-environment workspaces and a top-level state prefix to avoid collisions across clusters and upgrades; added migration scripts and Terraform import examples in scripts/ to help customers move existing resources into the new modules.

Upgrade notes (required reading for private installers): 1) Follow the scripts/migrate-state/README.md for stepwise import of node pools and IAM roles. 2) Run terraform plan against the new workspace prefix before apply; automated smoke tests are provided. 3) For GKE users with attached GPUs, ensure node pool autoscaling is disabled during migration window.

Rollback: modules include a lightweight compatibility layer (deprecated variables) that preserves previous naming for 1 release cycle to facilitate rollback. If a rollback is required after apply, follow the migration README to import resources back into the legacy layout.

Testing performed: unit tests for modules (terraform validate + tflint), integration smoke tests in perf-canary using a small private cluster, and an end-to-end upgrade run in staging. CI initially failed on tflint rule about aws_iam_policy naming; fix applied and CI passed.

Related: ENG-7421 tracks migration automation tasks. SUP-1122 is a customer-reported state drift issue that motivated rebuilding the state layout.

This PR is a net refactor (no behavior change for fresh installs); migration steps are required for existing customers.

release_notes: Consolidated Terraform modules for Private deployments: new gpu_node_pool, redwood_private_iam, and vpc_layout modules. Added migration/import scripts for upgrading existing private installations. No runtime changes for fresh installs. Follow scripts/migrate-state/README.md when upgrading existing clusters.
notes_for_ops: When rolling this into an on-prem/Private release, coordinate a migration window for customers with attached GPUs. Recommend a maintenance window and disable autoscaling on GPU node pools prior to import. State migration scripts are idempotent but test in staging first.
